name: Volume discount native
expected: Qty=300 Tripwire perpetual line receives tier-stepped per-unit price via PriceAdjustmentSchedule/PriceAdjustmentTier (1-100 band, 101-250 band, 251+ band); NetUnitPrice equals the 251+ band rate lower than 1-100 band rate.
actual: The native Volume Discount branch is unreachable in active V21 and cannot fire. (1) In the live V21 (run3 retrieve Jun 30 08:15, ExpressionSetDefinitionVersion 9QBWC0000000oWH4AY VersionNumber=21), every sub-block defines VolumePASIdConstant as the empty string ('') — so the VolumeDiscountEntries BKM lookup against Price_Adjustment_Tier_Decision_Table finds PriceAdjustmentScheduleId='' which matches no rows. Branch is a no-op regardless of gate conditions. (2) Org config: only 3 PriceAdjustmentSchedule records exist org-wide — 'Standard Attribute Based Adjustment' (84Xa50000010nWQEAY, ACTIVE, Attribute type), 'ZZ_E2E_RCA_20260613 Test Schedule' (84XWC000000S6bx2AC, INACTIVE), 'ZZ_E2E_Bundle_Sched_ZZ_E2E_RCA_20260613' (84XWC000000S6dZ2AS, INACTIVE). Zero active quantity-band (Volume) PriceAdjustmentSchedules. (3) Only 1 PriceAdjustmentTier exists org-wide: PAT-0000003633 (band 1-10, no Product2, belongs to inactive ZZ_E2E schedule). No multi-band 1-100/101-250/251+ tiers exist. (4) Actual volume/qty-tiered pricing is delivered via Attribute_Tier_Pricing_Storage__c (1154 rows) through the Attribute-based schedule — a different mechanism than the catalog's test_setup assumes.

defectStep: V21 step 'Volume Discount Entries' (VolumeDiscountEntries) + gate 'Volume Discounts' (VolumeDiscounts). VolumePASIdConstant='' makes the BKM lookup a no-op. This is NOT a defect — it is the intended design; Fortra uses the attribute-tier engine (Attribute_Tier_Pricing_Storage__c + Standard Attribute Based Adjustment schedule) for all quantity/volume tiers, not the native PriceAdjustmentSchedule/PriceAdjustmentTier path.
proposedFix: No fix required. The catalog test_setup should be re-characterized: 'Volume discount native (PriceAdjustmentTier path)' is intentionally unused in Fortra's pricing implementation. If native volume band discounting is ever desired, it would require: (a) creating an active Volume-type PriceAdjustmentSchedule with multi-band PriceAdjustmentTiers, and (b) setting VolumePASIdConstant in V21 to that schedule's Id. Current implementation routes all qty/volume tiers through Attribute_Tier_Pricing_Storage__c instead.
notes: Config/parity-class scenario. Carries over BLOCKED + EXPECTATION-ERROR verdict from run1 and run2. Re-verified on live V21 (run3 retrieve Jun 30 08:15) — no change: VolumePASIdConstant still empty, zero active Volume PriceAdjustmentSchedules, 1 org-wide PriceAdjustmentTier (inactive). Building a headless Qty=300 fixture would either (a) price through the attribute-tier path (not the named native mechanism) or (b) net $0 from the missing Tripwire perpetual PBE — neither constitutes evidence about the named V21 step. Verdict BLOCKED (named native mechanism untestable) with rootCause EXPECTATION-ERROR (catalog mischaracterized the mechanism as native PAS/PAT when it is actually Attribute_Tier_Pricing_Storage__c).
verdict_reason: Preflight fails: no active Volume-type PriceAdjustmentSchedule exists and VolumePASIdConstant='' in active V21, so the named native branch cannot fire. Cannot smoke-test a mechanism that does not exist in config. RootCause=EXPECTATION-ERROR because the catalog's test_setup describes a PriceAdjustmentSchedule/PriceAdjustmentTier qty-band mechanism that Fortra does not use; actual tiered pricing runs through Attribute_Tier_Pricing_Storage__c. Verdict BLOCKED, not FAIL — the procedure is not at fault.
